name: Accessibility for media
definition: Provide accessible formats and language support—captions/subtitles/transcripts, alt text, and multi‑language tracks—so content works for diverse audiences and aids SEO.

name: Accuracy, evidence, and independent verifiability
definition: All statements are correct and grounded in credible sources; provide citations/links (preferably to primary data) and enough detail for independent verification. Technical/scientific claims reflect the best evidence and context; facts/names/dates/figures are double‑checked; clearly label opinion vs. fact and avoid unverifiable or vague assertions.

name: Active voice
definition: Use active voice wherever possible for clarity, energy, and direct attribution.

name: Apology and acceptance of responsibility (with corrective steps)
definition: Promptly acknowledge the incident, accept responsibility without defensiveness or blame, offer a sincere, specific apology, and outline corrective actions.

name: Appropriate data visualization — type selection and usage
definition: Choose visualization types matched to data and goals (e.g., line/scatter/timeline/maps), applying visual channels appropriately to make complex information easy to grasp.

name: Assets pre‑attached to the release
definition: Upload and pre‑attach photos, video, and other media with the press release to reduce journalist effort and increase pickup.

name: Attribution and sourcing clarity (citations, links, credentials)
definition: Cite and link sources clearly, provide accessible evidence paths, and include speaker credentials/bios; avoid vague sourcing and reliance solely on the press release.

name: Audience and channel targeting and tailoring
definition: Define the primary audience and tailor message, tone, and format to that audience and to outlet/beat and channel norms.

name: Audience and outlet understanding, targeting, and tailoring
definition: Identify and segment priority publics and outlets; tailor messages, tone, framing, examples, and channels (incl. localization) to what each values while staying consistent overall.

name: Audience segmentation and targeting
definition: Identify and prioritize audience segments; tailor key messages, formats, channels, and language to each segment’s needs and preferences.

name: Audience targeting and relevance
definition: Define priority publics and tailor content to their needs and culture; make personal stakes and practical value explicit.

name: Audience understanding and tailoring
definition: Demonstrate clear understanding of target segments and align content, tone, packaging, and channels to their needs and context.

name: Audience-centric messaging and engagement
definition: Tailor content, tone, structure, and depth to audience needs and channels; make next steps obvious; respect journalists’ time while reassuring and explaining changes clearly.

name: Audience‑centric framing and value
definition: Frame around public/service value rather than self‑promotion, showing practical or emotional benefits for intended readers.

name: Authenticity and alignment between values, messaging, and actions
definition: Align communications, promises, DEI/cause messaging, and advertising with genuine commitments, operations, and data; avoid performative stunts or spin; ensure words, visuals, and experiences match reality and demonstrate sustained action.

name: Authoritative, newsworthy quotes and available spokespeople
definition: Include one or two substantive, attributable quotes from appropriate leaders/experts that add insight (including what’s unknown); ensure designated spokespeople are reachable for interviews.

name: Authority, third-party credibility, and social proof
definition: Build trust via credible senders, leadership voices, and independent third‑party validation; disclose credentials/affiliations; provide credible proof points and use social proof without misrepresentation.

name: Avoid deficit thinking and moralizing framings
definition: Avoid stigmatizing frames, alarmist metaphors, or normative leaps from data that distort understanding or blame individuals/groups.

name: Avoid overstatement and alarmism beyond evidence
definition: Do not exaggerate significance or use hyperbolic language that exceeds what the data support.

name: Avoid tone‑deaf or trivializing language
definition: Match tone and gravity to the issue; avoid wording or gestures that trivialize serious social issues or misread the moment.

name: Awards/milestones announcement effectiveness
definition: State the achievement clearly, explain significance, present measurable results, follow required formats, and supply relevant ceremony/context details.

name: Body provides supporting detail with clear flow
definition: After the lede, expand logically with background, data, and quotes that substantiate the news and explain the ‘why.’

name: Boilerplate and background with links
definition: Include concise organizational/author identity context and up‑to‑date links to official pages, newsroom, investor info, and helplines.

name: Boilerplate inclusion and quality
definition: Include a standard ‘About’ section that is current, accurate, and distinctive—succinctly covering mission, scope, credibility, and differentiators without generic claims or evasive language.

name: Boilerplate, company info, and publication metadata
definition: Include a complete, up‑to‑date About section and essential footer elements (company overview, affiliations, publication metadata, links, expert contacts).

name: Brand identity coherence and authenticity
definition: Align look, voice, and creative with authentic brand strategy and leadership voice; avoid forced tone shifts or superficial signal changes.

name: Broadcast-usable B‑roll provided
definition: Supply ready-to-air B‑roll clips (and related video/photography) prepared for broadcast use.

name: Broadcast‑ready B‑roll/VNR assets
definition: Supply professional, timely B‑roll and VNR packages with shot variety, stabilization, edit‑ready clips, spokesperson/interview options, and usable soundbites to save newsroom time.

name: Calls‑to‑action (CTA) effectiveness
definition: Provide clear, action‑oriented next steps matched to target audiences; use motivating, specific language to drive response or mobilization.

name: Candor about uncertainty, limitations, and tradeoffs
definition: Be candid about limits, open challenges, uncertainties, and tradeoffs; separate facts from speculation; situate findings within debate where relevant and disclose remediation steps.

name: Channel strategy and multi‑channel coordination
definition: Select the right media/channels, adapt versions/lengths to each, and coordinate consistent core messaging across touchpoints while accounting for channel‑specific risks.

name: Claim restraint and non-sensational language
definition: Keep wording specific and aligned with evidence; avoid exaggeration, implication leaps, clichéd superlatives, and sensational framings; ensure headlines/conclusions match the substantiated findings.

name: Clarity and conciseness
definition: Write clean, well‑structured copy that is brief yet complete, prioritizes clarity over style, and avoids filler.

name: Clarity and plain language
definition: Use simple, direct language and clear organization so diverse audiences can quickly understand key points.

name: Clarity, concision, and newsroom style
definition: State the main point directly; keep prose tight, active, factual, and front‑loaded; follow newsroom style and correctness; avoid dense copy and wordiness.

name: Clear calls to action and resource links
definition: Make one clear ask and provide obvious next steps with links to resources, demos, samples, contacts, or subscriptions.

name: Clear communication of uncertainty and preliminary status
definition: State what is known vs unknown, acknowledge preliminary status and major caveats, include confidence levels when appropriate, and set expectations early; separate facts from speculation.

name: Clear next steps and where to get help/info
definition: Provide explicit CTAs, instructions, and pointers to more information/resources tailored to the audience’s needs.

name: Clear, singular, effective call to action
definition: Present one unambiguous, benefit‑oriented action aligned to the content, with easy next steps that motivate meaningful response.

name: Company boilerplate completeness
definition: Provide a concise ‘About’ section with mission, history/scale, locations, key metrics, and relevant organizational context.

name: Comparative context and benchmarks
definition: Provide benchmarks and peer/baseline comparisons and situate the product/idea against alternatives, including advantages and trade‑offs.

name: Concrete commitments and follow‑through
definition: Make specific, credible commitments tied to values; explain oversight and revisions from feedback; show evidence of progress versus targets over time.

name: Concrete corrective actions and prevention
definition: Specify immediate steps taken and longer‑term safeguards to prevent recurrence; detail changes, investigations, and program improvements.

name: Concrete corrective and preventive actions (crises)
definition: When harm occurs, detail specific remedial steps, timelines, and systemic fixes that address root causes and prioritize safety.

name: Concrete evidence of value and impact
definition: Back claims with specific, comprehensible evidence—quantified benefits, clear stats/examples, and features‑to‑benefits translation.

name: Concrete quantitative detail
definition: Anchor the story with specific numbers and monetary figures, ideally early in the lede and reinforced in the body.

name: Consumer-facing clarity and disclosures
definition: Use precise naming/packaging language and disclose relevant costs (price, coverage, out‑of‑pocket) to prevent confusion and risk.

name: Content origin and AI transparency
definition: Disclose and verify the origin of content (in‑house vs agency, AI‑generated, etc.); explain how/when AI was used and its limits; avoid covert PR/astroturfing; ensure real, verifiable people and imagery.

name: Context and significance
definition: Provide necessary background and rationale so readers can interpret importance, trends, and implications.

name: Core news clarity, lede, and headlines
definition: Use the inverted pyramid with a tight lede; state the announcement and why it matters upfront; cover the Five Ws; provide 2–3 specific key messages; write clear, truthful headlines.

name: Core news structure and hierarchy (inverted pyramid)
definition: Craft a clear headline; prioritize the most newsworthy facts up top; use the inverted pyramid with logical flow that enables easy trimming.

name: Corrective and preventive actions to prevent recurrence
definition: Detail investigations/reviews, safeguards, and organizational changes to ensure the issue does not recur.

name: Crisis accountability, empathy, and corrective action
definition: Acknowledge harm and accept responsibility; apologize appropriately; communicate promptly via senior leaders; implement concrete corrective and preventive actions with timelines; report transparent progress and engage affected parties.

name: Crisis acknowledgement, apology, and amends
definition: Promptly acknowledge incidents, accept responsibility, offer specific apologies, and provide credible compensation/remediation mechanisms.

name: Crisis response speed and visibility
definition: Respond rapidly and visibly via public channels with clear acknowledgment and credible spokespeople; avoid delays and silence that fuel speculation.

name: Crisis response strategy and messaging coherence
definition: Align posture with responsibility/history; maintain a consistent strategy; avoid blame‑shifting, premature promises, or aggressive legal retaliation; provide clear explanations, facts known so far, and corrective actions; choose public vs. behind‑the‑scenes engagement deliberately and sustain updates.

name: Crisis strategy selection and execution (SCCT/CERC‑aligned)
definition: Select deny/diminish/rebuild strategies appropriate to crisis type and responsibility; communicate swiftly on the right channels with clear update cadence; account for media/social dynamics; acknowledge specific harms; pair messages with visible remedial/safety actions.

name: Cultural and historical sensitivity in messaging and creative
definition: Ensure names, imagery, humor, and tone are appropriate to cultural/historical context; avoid objectification, stereotypes, or messages that could be framed as disrespectful (including national/political sensitivities).

name: Cultural sensitivity, representation, and harm avoidance
definition: Anticipate cultural readings and current debates; avoid stereotypes/appropriation and prohibited or harmful content; engage authentically and mitigate misinterpretation risk.

name: Customer impact and transition details
definition: Clearly explain what changes for customers, what stays the same, timing, and support/transition arrangements.

name: Customer proof and measurable outcomes
definition: Use third‑party validation—named customers/partners, testimonials/logos, case outcomes—and concrete traction metrics to substantiate impact.

name: Data visualization and infographic design
definition: Choose and design charts/infographics for clarity and impact: appropriate chart types, disciplined content, readable hierarchy/typography, effective layout/colour, and interactive elements when useful.

name: Data visualization and infographic quality
definition: Use clear, accurate charts/diagrams with visual hierarchy, concise explanatory text, and built‑in context so readers quickly grasp meaning.

name: Data visualization effectiveness
definition: Select and design charts/infographics to highlight the key finding; follow data‑viz best practices for accuracy, hierarchy, color, and medium suitability.

name: Distribution, discoverability, and channel strategy
definition: Optimize subject/keywords, SEO/voice, and routing; adapt for owned/earned/social channels; follow distribution hygiene to aid newsroom processing and search.

name: Diverse voices and balanced perspectives
definition: Represent multiple relevant perspectives and sources (community, policy, researchers); reflect diversity across voices/formats; ensure accessibility where appropriate; acknowledge counter‑views for balanced coverage.

name: ESG/sustainability disclosure quality, comparability, and governance
definition: Provide specific, decision‑useful ESG/sustainability disclosures linked to financials; substantiate environmental claims; use recognized frameworks for comparability; cover governance oversight, material impacts, and value‑chain dependencies; avoid boilerplate and greenwashing.

name: Earned media measurement and analytics
definition: Define modern KPIs (EMV, mentions/citations/sentiment incl. social/influencer) and use tools to monitor and analyze coverage and outcomes.

name: Embeddability and reuse for media
definition: Provide excerptable, embeddable assets and structure content for easy reuse (slides, pull quotes, carousels) across outlets and owned channels.

name: Empathy and sensitivity in messaging
definition: Acknowledge human impact with clear, compassionate language; avoid self‑centered or tone‑deaf phrasing.

name: Empathy, apology, and ownership backed by action
definition: Respond promptly with a culturally respectful, empathetic tone; clearly acknowledge harm, accept responsibility (avoid blame‑shifting/euphemisms), apologize specifically, and pair words with credible corrective steps aligned with stated values.

name: Enable audience scrutiny and data literacy
definition: Help audiences interpret evidence and access/assess primary records by supplying datasets/source documents and interpretive guidance.

name: Event announcement essentials and media readiness
definition: Highlight agenda, speakers, logistics, and why it’s must‑attend; ensure broadcast‑friendly talent/availability to boost coverage.

name: Event/advisory essentials
definition: For event‑related releases, provide clear who/what/when/where logistics, notable guests/activities, and details that drive attendance and local interest.

name: Evidence, sourcing, and methods transparency
definition: Support claims with accurate, verifiable evidence; name/cite sources and link primary documents; disclose methods, data, assumptions, effect sizes, limitations, and validation so audiences can assess credibility and replicate where appropriate.

name: Evidence‑backed, specific, quantified claims
definition: Support assertions with specific, verifiable numbers and well‑sourced evidence; cite provenance so statistics survive editing and withstand scrutiny.

name: Explain why it matters
definition: Make the relevance to the intended audience explicit early—why it matters now and why readers should care; connect to trends where apt.

name: Explicit acknowledgment and sincere apology
definition: State clearly what went wrong and who was harmed; accept responsibility; apologize unambiguously and promptly; remove/stop offending content where warranted.

name: External expert/third‑party validation
definition: Increase credibility via independent experts, reputable institutions, and other credible third‑party endorsements or corroboration.

name: Format and genre fit to news conventions
definition: Match document type and objective news style to newsroom conventions (e.g., release vs advisory/alert) so copy is editor‑ready.

name: Founder/CEO voice strategy
definition: Use a distinct founder/executive voice intentionally to differentiate the brand, add credibility, and strengthen narrative cohesion.

name: Framing, media-ecosystem, and optics awareness
definition: Recognize how media frames and incentives shape coverage and stakeholder perception; choose defensible frames strategically and anticipate scrutiny and optics beyond mere legal defensibility.

name: Funding announcement best practices
definition: Lead with the substantive ‘what’s being built’ and the surprising fact; cite credible investors; include demos/beta access and structured quotes; avoid generic headlines.

name: Headline and lede effectiveness
definition: Headlines and opening lines hook interest and deliver immediate value with an active, specific summary (tweetable headline, strong dek/lede, clear dateline), avoiding generic phrasing.

name: Headline and subhead effectiveness
definition: Craft specific, news‑hooked headlines and subheads that succinctly summarize key outcomes (use numbers when helpful) and supply brief summaries when outlets request them.

name: Headline effectiveness
definition: Headline is captivating, concise, specific, and format-appropriate; it captures the key claim/angle and follows newsroom conventions.

name: Headline effectiveness and integrity
definition: Headlines are brief and compelling, surface the key finding/impact, are SEO‑ and reader‑optimized, include required elements (e.g., dateline when applicable), and avoid clickbait.

name: Headline is concise and clearly summarizes the news
definition: Provide a short, eye‑catching headline that immediately communicates the main announcement.

name: Headline/subject line effectiveness
definition: Craft clear, concise, news‑first headlines/subjects that summarize the core action, parties, and relevance; signal news value without sensationalism and drive opens.

name: Headline/topline clarity and accuracy
definition: Craft clear, accurate, specific headlines/decks that foreground the substantive news and match tone to the underlying results.

name: Human, humble spokesperson tone
definition: Ensure spokesperson quotes sound natural, respectful, and unboastful rather than canned or grandiose.

name: Identification and complete media contacts
definition: Clearly attribute the issuer and provide accurate, prominent media contact details and roles so the item is directly usable.

name: Impartial, nonpartisan presentation
definition: Maintain objectivity and neutral wording; avoid partisan framing; attribute viewpoints and represent relevant sides fairly.

name: Inclusive, non‑discriminatory, bias‑aware language
definition: Use inclusive, respectful language that avoids stigma, stereotypes, and biased idioms; apply people‑first/identity‑first per community preference and gender‑neutral forms where appropriate.

name: Inclusive, respectful representation and cultural sensitivity
definition: Use inclusive, non‑stigmatizing language and authentic representation; respect culture and self‑identification; avoid discriminatory/inflammatory framing and tokenism; ensure accessible formats.

name: Information architecture and scannability
definition: Use clear headings/subheads, bullets, and descriptive links to structure topical chunks and make content quickly scannable.

name: Interactive and animated explainers
definition: Employ interactive/animated formats (e.g., step‑throughs, dashboards) to explain complex data, mechanisms, or processes.

name: Investor communications clarity and compliance
definition: Provide material, compliant disclosures on strategy, performance, risks, and deal terms; align market expectations with analyst‑grade clarity; integrate required risk disclosures and manage legal/disclosure risks.

name: Investor communications quality and relevance
definition: Communicate strategy, viability, and long‑term outlook to investors in concise, decision‑oriented formats that build confidence.

name: Investor communications readiness and accessibility
definition: Maintain robust IR infrastructure/materials and communicate performance and strategy in plain, forward‑looking, investor‑oriented language.

name: Investor‑relations trust‑building and value story
definition: Sustain investor confidence through clear, customized engagement and a coherent value narrative; integrate ESG where relevant; analyze operational drivers, anticipate Q&A needs, and pre‑frame negative news responsibly.

name: Journalist usability and information subsidy
definition: Provide press‑ready materials and the elements reporters value (clear angles, proofs, quotable sources/contacts) while respecting newsroom independence and formats.

name: Journalistic, non-promotional orientation
definition: Present information in a neutral, newsroom‑appropriate voice that prioritizes public interest and genuine news value over puffery; do not masquerade PR as independent journalism.

name: Journalist‑centric targeting and pitching
definition: Match topics, style, depth, and assets to outlet/reporter beats and their audience; personalize thoughtfully; meet media formatting/timing needs to earn coverage.

name: Journalist‑centric targeting, personalization, and packaging
definition: Match beats/outlets; personalize subject lines and openings with an original, reader‑valuable angle; write for reporter needs and target formats; avoid mass/promotional blasts.

name: Journalist‑ready packaging and media facilitation
definition: Anticipate editors’ questions; provide contacts and next steps; supply rights‑cleared, correctly formatted materials; respect media formats/deadlines; make kits standalone and wire‑ready.

name: Keywords and tags for SEO
definition: Use relevant searchable keywords in headlines/summaries and natural copy (including boilerplate when appropriate) and apply correct topical tagging.

name: Launch/re‑launch campaign category
definition: Work created to launch or relaunch a product or service.

name: Lead with complete 5Ws and impact
definition: Open with a lead that compresses who/what/when/where/why (with dateline where relevant), concrete details (names/dates/numbers), and audience impact.

name: Lead with what matters (inverted pyramid)
definition: Put the most newsworthy facts and implications first, followed by supporting detail in standard inverted‑pyramid order.

name: Leadership visibility and accountability in crises
definition: Ensure senior leaders are visible, take responsibility, and engage directly with stakeholders during crises to humanize the response and signal accountability.

name: Lead‑first inverted pyramid and information hierarchy
definition: Prioritize the most important information first with a strong lede; make relationships clear and structure for skimmability and human/machine parsing.

name: Lede effectiveness and inverted‑pyramid structure
definition: Open with a concise, news‑first lede that answers the 5Ws/How and stakes; front‑load key facts and use an inverted pyramid flow, placing quotes/background later.

name: Lede quality and completeness (5Ws and key news)
definition: The opening immediately conveys the core news and why it matters, covering the Five Ws (and how/method when relevant) with key numbers/context.

name: Lede summarizes the news concisely
definition: The first paragraph crisply delivers the core who/what/when/why and principal result in one clear sentence.

name: Legal, safety, and disclaimer compliance
definition: Include required legal notices and precise disclaimers; avoid unauthorized associations and unsafe encouragement; add necessary backgrounders/timelines.

name: Limitations and uncertainty communication
definition: Clearly distinguish known vs. speculative; state study/report limitations, scope, external validity, and realistic timelines; include appropriate disclaimers; situate findings within prior evidence/consensus.

name: Local relevance and geographic context
definition: Surface proximity and place: specify where programs/events occur, add geographic context, and frame community relevance for local outlets.

name: Local relevance and market targeting
definition: Localize content and variants to increase community/regional news value; highlight concrete local/practical relevance and market‑specific angles.

name: Local/regional angle and proximity
definition: Clearly articulate locally relevant angles, impacts, or identity hooks for the target market/outlet.

name: Localization and cultural adaptation
definition: Adapt language, tone, references, and examples for each market; go beyond literal translation by using local voices/data and explaining local references; provide localized versions where appropriate.

name: Media access and follow-up
definition: Remove access barriers and make follow‑up easy: no paywalls; clear, reachable contacts; boilerplate/mission; links to resources/background; and complete story packages with full/dual contact details where relevant.

name: Message consistency and non‑contradiction
definition: Convey a coherent, accurate narrative over time across channels, documents, and spokespeople; avoid conflicting statements and ensure framing matches situation severity.

name: Message framing and key‑point coherence
definition: Lead with one clear primary angle and coherent frame; maintain alignment across headline/lead/quotes; foreground meaningful differentiation and answer ‘so what?’.

name: Message–reality alignment and cross-channel consistency
definition: Ensure messages and tone align with real actions and values; maintain a coherent narrative across internal/external channels and over time; update narratives as facts change; avoid conflicting signals.

name: Mobile optimization and performance
definition: Design and test pages/assets for mobile-first consumption with responsive layouts, legible graphics, and fast-loading, optimized media.

name: Multimedia assets: availability, quality, and usability
definition: Provide high‑quality, rights‑cleared photos/video/graphics; optimize files for web; include captions/credits; link (don’t attach); ensure assets are downloadable/embeddable and easy for newsrooms to use.

name: Multimedia assets: quality, relevance, and storytelling
definition: Provide high‑quality, relevant visuals/audio that are designed for clarity, easy reuse, and immediate storytelling impact without overwhelming the content.

name: Multimedia included (avoid text‑only)
definition: Include high‑quality, rights‑cleared visuals (photos, video, infographics, audio) to strengthen the story and avoid text‑only releases.

name: Neutral, non‑promotional newsroom tone
definition: Write in an objective, journalism‑like voice; avoid hype, sales copy, superlatives, and sensationalism while fairly presenting facts and expertise.

name: News value and angle strength
definition: Present a strong, timely, trend‑aligned angle that makes editors/audiences care and offers credible pickup potential.

name: Newsroom‑ready packaging and pickup readiness
definition: Reduce newsroom friction with reusable copy, verified resources, and plug‑and‑play materials so editors can publish with minimal callbacks or rewrites.

name: Newsworthiness, angle, and context
definition: Ensure the announcement is timely and meaningful beyond the issuer; frame a clear, compelling angle; explain implications and connect to industry trends; include an easy verification path.

name: Newsworthiness, novelty, and hook/angle selection
definition: Anchor the story in strong, timely hooks and the most newsworthy angle; demonstrate real impact/novelty, cultural fit, continuity potential, and clear audience interest.

name: Newsworthiness, timeliness, and angle strength
definition: Anchor the release in a compelling, timely hook aligned to classic news values and audience/editorial fit; avoid vanity or inside‑baseball non‑news.

name: News‑first lede clarity
definition: Deliver the core announcement (5Ws/impact) immediately in the lede, suitable for direct‑to‑public reading.

name: Non‑promotional, journalistic news tone
definition: Write in an informative, journalistic tone—not like an advertisement or hype copy.

name: Ongoing transparency and progress reporting
definition: Commit to ongoing public reporting of reviews, reforms, outcomes, and performance; publish corrective actions, culture metrics, repositories, and progress updates with honest assessment over time.

name: Opening hook effectiveness
definition: The opening uses a strong hook (e.g., vivid image, quote, question) that quickly signals what’s newly possible and draws readers into the inverted‑pyramid structure.

name: Openness and media access/responsiveness
definition: Provide access to information, documents, and experts; allow questioning and answer candidly; be responsive and non‑hostile; correct errors transparently to support independent reporting.

name: Original research/data as newsworthy content
definition: Publish proprietary, novel, or industry‑defining data/reports to create inherent news hooks that earn coverage and backlinks.

name: Originality and substantive new information
definition: Contains unique, useful information that enables differentiated coverage and delivers public importance or novelty; avoids duplication.

name: Outlet/beat targeting and personalization
definition: The angle and materials are tightly matched to the outlet/section and reporter’s beat and audience, with individualized references and appropriate tailoring.

name: Overall newsworthiness and clear hook
definition: The item passes newsroom judgment with a compelling, outlet‑relevant angle; it’s substantive, novel/impactful, timely, clearly relevant, and avoids vanity announcements.

name: Owned newsroom hub with topical navigation
definition: Present releases on branded hubs with topical tags, categories, and filters to aid discovery and navigation.

name: PR origin disclosure and anti‑churnalism
definition: Disclose when content derives from press releases/PR and the extent of PR input; avoid copy‑paste uptake; encourage independent scrutiny and original verification.

name: Packaging design effectiveness and shelf recognition
definition: Ensure packages are easy to find and choose with distinctive, validated designs that retain expected brand cues while balancing innovation.

name: Partner/customer voices and social proof
definition: Leverage partners, coalitions, and customer testimony to extend reach and substantiate claims via trusted intermediaries.

name: Partnership announcement essentials and credibility
definition: Clearly state the collaboration’s purpose, each party’s contributions, and concrete benefits; ensure named partners add credibility and relevance.

name: Pitch construction and distribution strategy
definition: Craft concise, value‑driven pitches (include crisp methodology when relevant) and use tier‑appropriate distribution, angle selection, and calendar alignment.

name: Pitch personalization and outlet fit
definition: Personalize outreach by referencing the journalist/outlet’s recent work and voice, targeting the right venues, and tailoring the angle/opening to their beat.

name: Plain language and minimal jargon/clichés
definition: Use clear, accessible language for intended audiences; avoid or define technical terms; drop insider buzzwords and clichés.

name: Plain language, readability, and accessibility
definition: Use clear, concise, jargon‑free language and reader‑friendly structure so intended audiences can understand on first pass; define terms, avoid idioms, and ensure linguistic/cultural accessibility.

name: Plain, concise, engaging writing
definition: Write in clear, jargon‑free prose with tight focus, varied yet controlled sentences, and high information density; every sentence advances the news.

name: Press assets and visual communication
definition: Provide a complete, accessible media kit with clean, downloadable assets and proper branding; ensure scannable structure and include high‑quality, accurately labeled visuals and clear data visualizations.

name: Press kit and background resources for journalists
definition: Provide a journalist‑friendly kit/dossier bundling the release with key facts, backgrounders, images, and other reusable assets.

name: Press kit completeness and distribution
definition: Assemble/distribute a complete press kit with backgrounders, fact sheets, company history, sources, and links to assets in outlet‑preferred formats (including wire readiness).

name: Press release structure and components
definition: Use a clear, journalist‑friendly structure with strong lead, supporting proof points/methods, quotes, and essential details (5Ws/H, legal/background).

name: Press release types and event essentials
definition: Use the correct release/asset type and, for events, provide clear logistics and speaker/agenda details to enable promotion.

name: Press-ready multimedia asset package
definition: Embedded and/or downloadable press-ready images, video, audio, and documents are provided (woven into the copy or as a media kit) so newsrooms can use them immediately.

name: Press‑release SEO optimization
definition: Apply on‑page SEO best practices (structure, metadata, copy, rich media) so the release is discoverable in search and Google News.

name: Professional newsroom style and consistency
definition: Follow AP/newsroom style with correct grammar and usage, applying a consistent style guide; write objectively and copy‑ready.

name: Public affairs/media relations roles and appropriate instruments
definition: Define PA/PIO responsibilities and strategy; select the right vehicle (release, advisory, PSA, funding/company news); provide timely compliance alerts; clarify the purpose of releases in informing stakeholders.

name: Public- and beneficiary-focused framing
definition: Emphasize public benefit and real‑world impact for beneficiaries rather than organizational self‑promotion; avoid boilerplate superlatives and canned quotes.

name: Public‑interest orientation and fairness to stakeholders
definition: Prioritize genuine public/beneficiary impact and ethics over self‑promotion; treat stakeholders fairly; clearly state purpose and public benefit; help hold power to account.

name: Public‑safety and risk communication
definition: Prioritize stakeholder safety; explain potential harms and tradeoffs; provide actionable protective guidance and credible resources; acknowledge/manage rumors; account for existing beliefs; ensure accessible channels; engage affected groups with tangible steps.

name: Quote inclusion, sourcing, and substance
definition: Include quotable, attributable statements—ideally from authorized leaders or experts—that add new insight and specifics (often with numbers), avoid platitudes, and, when useful, provide multiple perspectives.

name: Quote quality, authenticity, and value
definition: Use named, authoritative speakers; quotes sound human (not PR/legalese) and add new, specific information or perspective.

name: Quote quality, sourcing, and usefulness
definition: Include a small set of quotable, role‑appropriate voices (internal and—when apt—independent) that add new insight and are easy to excerpt.

name: Quote strategy, quality, and execution
definition: Include early, substantive, authentic quotes from appropriate voices that add new information/context/emotion, are concise and quotable, and are placed/packaged for reuse.

name: Rebrand strategy and respect for brand equity
definition: Rebrand only with clear strategic rationale; preserve iconic equity and public attachment where prudent, acknowledging identity’s cultural role.

name: Rebrand strategy coherence and naming/usability
definition: Ground rebrands in strategy and consumer insight; preserve valuable equities and align naming/UX with entrenched semantics and user expectations.

name: Rebrand/identity change communications
definition: Communicate the rationale and manage change carefully—preserving or thoughtfully evolving distinctive cues and respecting existing equity and attachments.

name: Related links, sources, and navigational coherence
definition: Provide clear links to background, sources/citations, and follow‑ups; use subheads and coherent linking so readers can explore implications.

name: Risk and public-health communication with actionable guidance
definition: Provide accessible, evidence‑based risk/benefit information and specific, feasible protective actions; explain rationales to motivate behavior change and manage infodemics during emergencies.

name: SEO/discoverability for releases
definition: Optimize releases for discoverability (descriptive anchors, alt text, structured metadata, newsroom‑hosted pages) for both search and AI; avoid forced keyword stuffing.

name: Scannable formatting and layout
definition: Make key points extractable at a glance with short paragraphs/sentences, subheads, bullets, white space, and mobile‑friendly structure.

name: Scannable, media‑friendly formatting
definition: Use headers, bullets, short paragraphs, minimalist layouts, and visual highlights so journalists can quickly locate core facts and next steps.

name: Science communication best practices and engagement
definition: Translate findings accessibly using evidence‑based SciComm; balance rigor with journalistic usability; set goals that enable informed decisions and mutual learning among publics and policymakers.

name: Scientific accuracy, causality, and context
definition: Communicate evidence precisely—situate findings among alternatives, avoid causal overreach, include baselines and counterfactuals, and frame clinical/practical relevance appropriately.

name: Scientific rigor, accuracy, and uncertainty communication
definition: Match claims to evidence; avoid causal overreach and novelty hype; quantify appropriately (e.g., effect sizes, probabilities); report safety/harms and replication needs; distinguish consensus vs frontier and preprint/animal vs human applicability; state limitations clearly.

name: Search and algorithmic discoverability
definition: Optimize headlines, body, links, and asset metadata for search and emerging AI/aggregator surfaces; use relevant keywords, descriptive filenames/alt text, and distribution that earns reputable backlinks.

name: Situate findings within prior evidence
definition: Explain whether the work is new or a replication and how it fits within existing studies/consensus so readers grasp novelty vs. confirmation.

name: Social media engagement, listening, and amplification risk
definition: Use social platforms for timely, conversational updates and listening; monitor and acknowledge backlash; manage narratives and recognize amplification risks from executive/brand posts.

name: Social/digital platform optimization
definition: Adapt content and assets to social platforms and their algorithms; produce platform‑native versions (e.g., short video), leverage partnerships, and drive reach/engagement.

name: Source transparency, attribution, and justified anonymity
definition: Attribute sources and speakers; prefer named sources; disclose conflicts and credentials; justify and explain any anonymity; rely on independently verifiable, multi‑sourced information.

name: Specific corrective, preventive, and compensatory actions
definition: In crises, detail concrete fixes and preventive steps (investigations, policy/training changes, reorganizations), direct remedies/reassurances, and plans to compensate and protect affected stakeholders.

name: Specific, complete, checkable facts and claims
definition: Provide concrete, verified details (5Ws/H, methods, metrics, partners, pricing/availability) so statements are specific and testable.

name: Specific, meaningful metrics and performance context
definition: Include concrete, credible numbers and meaningful KPIs that substantiate claims; add context (comparisons, drivers); avoid vanity metrics.

name: Specific, measurable commitments and follow‑through
definition: Replace vague pledges with concrete, time‑bound actions and metrics; report ongoing progress over promises.

name: Specificity and concreteness
definition: Claims are supported with concrete, specific facts and examples; abstract statements are clarified with tangible details.

name: Spokesperson and third‑party credibility (substantive quotes)
definition: Feature credible, sufficiently senior spokespeople and independent experts appropriately; include substantive quotes and provide on‑the‑record access.

name: Spokesperson credibility and authority
definition: Use named representatives with clear ownership and relevant expertise; surface senior leadership when appropriate.

name: Sponsorship, funding, and conflict‑of‑interest disclosure
definition: Clearly identify the communicator and purpose; fully disclose sponsors, funding, relevant relationships, and conflicts of interest; label PR/paid materials to avoid confusion with independent news; properly attribute quotes, facts, and data.

name: State limitations and caveats
definition: Explicitly state study or claim limitations and appropriate caveats to guide accurate interpretation.

name: Study limitations and caveats disclosed
definition: Explicitly state design/measurement limits and generalizability so readers can gauge the strength and boundaries of findings.

name: Subheadline (dek) — presence, function, and SEO
definition: A one- to two-sentence subhead (dek) appears under the headline, adds new context/teaser or key facts, bridges to the lede, and incorporates secondary keywords mindful of SERP use.

name: Subject line effectiveness
definition: Email subject lines are compelling, specific, and personalized (without clickbait), include concrete entities/numbers where useful, and are tested or iterated for performance.

name: Substantiated environmental/ESG claims (no greenwashing)
definition: Make environmental/ESG assertions only when specific, current, and independently verifiable; avoid vague aspirations, unverifiable “firsts,” or aspirational misrepresentation.

name: Support claims with relevant data and sourcing
definition: Back assertions with pertinent, contextualized statistics and links; cite sources and provide enough methodological detail for credibility.

name: Swift remediation and restitution
definition: Act quickly to contain harm and make affected parties whole (e.g., recalls, fixes, compensation, interim support).

name: Tailored versions for outlets/segments
definition: Create tailored versions of the release/pitch for different outlets, sections, journalists, and audience segments.

name: Third‑party allies, coalitions, and opinion leaders
definition: Identify and mobilize credible independent allies/opinion leaders to echo key points, offer contactable validation, and expand reach/credibility.

name: Timeliness and recency signaled
definition: The announcement is genuinely new, pegged to a timely development, and clearly signals recency to audiences and editors.

name: Timely, frequent, transparent updates
definition: Acknowledge issues quickly; disclose core facts promptly; admit uncertainty when present; coordinate messaging and maintain promised update cadence across channels; avoid going silent.

name: Tone and voice alignment
definition: Maintain a courteous, professional tone aligned to brand and audience while remaining human and readable.

name: Translate technical/scientific content for lay readers
definition: Interpret complex advances in accessible language, define non‑common knowledge, and provide relevant context for non‑experts.

name: Truthful, evidence‑grounded claims
definition: Stick to verifiable facts; avoid speculation; use careful, precise wording supported by defensible evidence.

name: Truthfulness, correction, and non-suppression of material facts
definition: Do not make false or misleading claims (by commission or omission); do not hide or obscure material facts; correct your own errors promptly and visibly; proactively address external misinformation.

name: Truthfulness, substantiation, and non‑deception (no hype/manipulation)
definition: Ensure all claims are accurate and verifiable; avoid spin, hype, and misleading or unsubstantiated assertions; forbid fabrication, fake content, undisclosed sponsorships, covert manipulation/astroturfing, and disguised advocacy; publish prompt, clear corrections.

name: Two-way stakeholder and community engagement
definition: Invite input and sustain relationships with stakeholders/affected communities on and offline; manage hostility professionally; co‑produce responses to build trust and long‑term reputation.

name: Two‑way stakeholder engagement, inclusion, and trust restoration
definition: Identify affected audiences; listen and respond to concerns; respect public values and self‑identification; involve communities/partners; disclose engagement activities; and use ongoing dialogue and support to rebuild trust.

name: Use credible authority and unique access as proof points
definition: Support assertions with credible evidence and appropriately invoke named experts/founders/insiders to add context and credibility without overstating certainty.

name: Use proprietary/original data to create news
definition: Publish proprietary research or trend data that generates newsworthy, reusable content and positions the organization with unique insight.

name: Value proposition and competitive differentiation
definition: Translate capabilities into clear, compelling benefits; articulate distinctiveness vs competitors; ensure creative links directly to product value.

name: Visual design for readability and contrast
definition: Use layout, grid, typography, and color/contrast to ensure legibility, clear hierarchy, and appropriate tone.

name: Visual storytelling quality and integration
definition: Use high‑quality, purposeful visuals (photos/video/charts/UX) integrated with text to clarify complex points, advance the narrative, and add appropriate emotion/immersion.

name: Visual/media assets quality and readiness
definition: Supply high‑quality, appropriately credited visuals and press‑ready asset packs with honest, clear information design to enable immediate newsroom use.

name: Wire‑ready professional format
definition: Use AP style and consistent, publication‑ready formatting to reduce editing burden and signal professionalism.

name: Writing clarity, mechanics, and voice quality
definition: Favor concrete, energetic prose with strong verbs; ensure grammatical correctness, eliminate redundancy, and maintain a conversational, authentic voice.
